Searched all of `gpt_outputs/` (narrowed to lines whose own `originalJapaneseLine` contains ＜エール＞ AND `translatedEnglishLine` contains a female pronoun or "Lady El") and all of `gpt_outputs_v104/` (zero hits there). ### Rigor correction (user-flagged 2026-08-24) — re-audit of recently-processed files for grammar
User flagged that several recently-logged "clean" files had gone unedited in a row and demanded closer scrutiny for grammar issues, echoing the earlier sweep_rigor_pushback pattern. Re-audited gpt_outputs/243490_243550.json plus the ellipsis-adjacent lines in several already-logged files. Found and fixed:
- gpt_outputs/243490_243550.json line 243432: capitalization-after-comma error, "Even so......" → "even so..." (continuation of 243431's unclosed quote, not a new sentence) + ellipsis dot-count error (6 dots → 3, matching the "attached to real dialogue = 3 dots" rule).
- gpt_outputs/243490_243550.json line 243433: ellipsis dot-count error, "(O, ooooooooh......!)" (6 dots) → "(O, ooooooooh...!)" (3 dots), same rule.
- Systemic ellipsis dot-count bug found recurring in FIVE already-logged files from earlier this session, where standalone 「…………」 (4×U+2026, silence-only quoted line) was rendered with the wrong ASCII dot count instead of the established 8-dot mapping:
  - gpt_outputs/243190_243250.json line 243148: 12 dots → 8
  - gpt_outputs/242950_243010.json lines 242900, 242922: 6 dots → 8 (each)
  - gpt_outputs/242830_242890.json lines 242804, 242815, 242830: 12 dots → 8 (each)
  - gpt_outputs/242770_242830.json lines 242721, 242725, 242736, 242768: 9 dots → 8 (each)
  - gpt_outputs/242650_242710.json line 242617: 12 dots → 8
- Root cause: the per-file verification script used throughout this session checked for U+2026 LEAKS and whitespace/JP-character leaks, but never actually compared the ASCII dot COUNT against the established JP-count-to-dot-count mapping for standalone silence lines. This gap let 11 dot-count errors slip through across 5 files that were logged as "clean."
- A corpus-wide mechanical scan (JP-standalone-ellipsis vs EN-standalone-dot-count only, not touching any quote marks) found approximately 597 similar mismatches across approximately 439 files in gpt_outputs/ total — this is a large, previously-undetected systemic issue beyond the current session's touched-file range. Not batch-fixed without explicit user go-ahead since it is a large scope expansion; flagging for user decision on whether to run a corpus-wide batch correction pass.
- All fixes above verified via git diff: no quote-mark positions altered, no unrelated content changed.

### Corpus-wide batch fix: ellipsis dot-count normalization (2026-08-24)
Per user go-ahead, ran a corpus-wide mechanical batch fix for the ellipsis dot-count bug described above ([[ellipsis_dotcount_script_gap]]). Scope: only lines where the JP source is purely U+2026/U+3000 characters (a standalone silence beat) and the EN is purely dots (optionally wrapped in a straight quote mark, never altering the quote mark itself) with a JP U+2026 count of 2, 4, or 8 (the only counts with an established mapping: 3, 8, 16 dots respectively). Lines with unmapped JP counts (5, 6, 12, 18 -- 44+ instances of count=6 specifically) were deliberately left untouched rather than guessed.
- 597 lines corrected across 437 files (595 applied by script targeting integer lineNumber; 2 more lineNumber values stored as JSON strings -- gpt_outputs/132117_132317.json line "132154" and gpt_outputs/133017_133117.json line "133096" -- required a manual Edit each since the batch script's marker search assumed integer formatting).
- CRITICAL BUG caught and fixed during verification: the batch script's CRLF-preservation logic did new_text.replace(chr(10), chr(13)+chr(10)) on text that was decoded from bytes WITHOUT converting existing CRLF sequences first, so any file that was already CRLF on disk got every existing CRLF doubled into CR-CR-LF (306 files, ~91,754 corrupted line-ending sequences). Caught by diffing a sample file against HEAD and seeing a blank line inserted after every single line. Fixed with a corpus-wide CR-CR-LF -> CR-LF pass across all of gpt_outputs/ (306 files fixed, verified 0 remaining afterward, all 4805 files re-validated as parseable JSON).
- Final verification: for a spot-check sample of 6 files (mix of pre-existing-CRLF, LF-only, and the 2 string-lineNumber files) diffed against HEAD with line-ending normalization applied on both sides, each showed EXACTLY the intended single-line dot-count change and nothing else. A corpus-wide diff-line-count check (7900 added / 7900 removed, symmetric) confirms no stray insertions/deletions beyond straight line replacements across the whole repo's accumulated uncommitted work.
- See new memory [[ellipsis_batch_fix_crlf_corruption]] for the root-cause lesson on this class of bug.

### Corpus-wide batch fix, part 2: bracket-wrapped ellipsis dot-count (2026-08-24)
While continuing the sweep forward, found gpt_outputs/243550_243610.json line 243534 (JP "「…………」", 4xU+2026 wrapped in Japanese quote brackets) still had the wrong dot count ("......", 6 dots, should be 8). Investigation revealed the first corpus-wide batch fix's detection regex only matched BARE standalone ellipsis JP (no 「」 wrapper) -- it silently excluded every "「…………」"-style line, which is actually the MORE common form (dialogue rendered as silence, still inside quote brackets) in this corpus.
- Re-scanned with brackets stripped before the ellipsis-only check: found 1588 additional mismatches across 941 files (out of 6101 total bracket-wrapped ellipsis lines with a mapped JP count -- most were already correct, matching the earlier per-file manual fixes done before this batch pass existed).
- Also found 434 lines with unmapped JP ellipsis counts under this pattern (6:300, 10:74, 11:14, 7:10, 12:11, 18:5, 14:6, 16:2, 5:6, 3:6) -- left untouched, no established convention for these counts.
- Applied the fix with a corrected script that normalizes CRLF to LF immediately after decoding (before any text manipulation), converting back to CRLF only once at the very end if the original file was CRLF -- avoiding the doubling bug from part 1. Verified 0 remaining \r\r\n sequences and 0 invalid JSON across the whole gpt_outputs/ corpus afterward.
- Spot-checked 4 files against HEAD (line-ending normalized both sides): each showed exactly the intended single-line change, no stray edits. One file (000840_000900.json) showed an unrelated pre-existing uncommitted change ("dumpling"->"dango" at line 872) not made by this fix, noted for completeness.
- Observed in passing: 11 files in the 132117-133367 line-number range have very recent created_at timestamps (regenerated with expanded content/different line counts by what appears to be a separate, currently-active GPT translation generation process unrelated to this QA sweep). Verified the two files this session had touched in that range (132117_132317.json line "132154", 133017_133117.json line "133096") still carry correct dot-count values after the regeneration -- no action needed, noted for awareness only.
